data.note: rails-red is a MEASUREMENT here, not a claim: every new rail was copied onto main and run there. All fifteen door and scope cases fail on main. Thirteen failed at the first measurement; the two that passed were hollow (a time-pin case asserting only a clock, and a re-consent case whose fallback was the clock rather than the scope) and both were strengthened until they fail there too. The guards whose behaviour was already on main were measured by REVERT PROBE instead: deleting boundGroundFor's strike filter reddens the separate-posture case, deleting the channel guard reddens the channel refusal, deleting the container guard reddens the dropped-container case and reproduces the finding exactly (the write lands, the read refuses), restoring the one-link strike test reddens the three-link chain, and reverting whoami's note reddens the note assertion. Two CLI probes likewise: removing the pool backend factory reddens the ledger case, removing the pool strike reddens the revoke case.

S1's whole rail set, all six on main. Frozen-rail edits went through the two-PR ceremony twice: six phase-15 rails declared in #529 for #526 and spent in #530, then three declared in #532 for #533. Each rehearsed EXEMPT against its declaration and red against main from the same tree.
format + lint + typecheck + build + all tests, run ALONE at the landing revision

the slice landed as a stack of eight PRs (#525 library, #529 declaration, #526 doors, #530 spend, #527 docs, #528 landing, #532 declaration, #533 audit round two), each re-barred after every fold; this branch carries the evidence and the archive

data.command: adlc hollow-test --test-cmd 'npx vitest run <killer suites>' --base origin/main
data.note: diff-scoped mutation runs at each slice's final revision: the library seam 14 total / 12 killed / 2 survived (both folded into the rail, then clean), the doors 9/6/3 then 8/6/2 then 8/7/1 as each survivor earned a rail or was named, the landing 8/7/1, and the audit's round two 2/1/1. Two survivors are named rather than chased: whoami's gateway-undefined arm, which no caller can reach because every door resolves its mount first, and the negation walk's cycle guard, which no input can reach because a delta id is a content address, so a delta can only point at one that already exists and a mutual pair cannot be built.

dryEvidence: loam-hollow-rail, in fresh contexts across two review workflows and five rounds. It found the library's H1 case green with its own guard deleted (its fixture was shared-posture, where containerScope's own closure carries the strike, so a separate-posture case was added and the filter pinned), the channel-lens refusal unrailed anywhere, the app and byte door control unable to tell a working door from one refusing everyone, the pair-revoke case guaranteed by its own stub, and the ticket's new rails undeclared. Every one folded. The author's own rails-red measurement then caught two hollow cases the lenses had read and passed, which is why that measurement is now doctrine. dryEvidence: loam-lens-name and loam-scan-scale, fresh contexts, two rounds. Confirmed and folded: the CLI ledger derived a bound connection's standing from the primary and reported a live connection as holding none, while whoami read the pool and reported the opposite; whoami's own note promised a write beside its own write:false; the bound listing's cost was documented O(scope) where the call is O(ground), and paid again per listed entity. The cost findings are stated in the code rather than optimised, and a per-container candidate set is named as S2's work. Every threaded value was checked for kind: identity.actor is a seed while the append fence compares authors, a container and an inbox are never confused, and each door that cannot scope refuses by name.

dryEvidence: loam-suppression and loam-erasure, fresh contexts, two rounds, with a verifier per finding refuting 28 of 39. Confirmed and folded: loam grant revoke printed a strike it no longer performed and never touched the grant that is a bound connection's standing (H7, plus a stranded live grant); a bound write survived the drop of its container, landing durably while the door reported failure and every retry minted another delta; the struck-strike test was one link where the substrate's is recursive, so a claim revived when its strike's strike was struck; the append door's 403 swallowed a transient that tells the caller to retry; the byte door's refusal carried no CORS header, so a browser saw an opaque error instead of the sentence. Cross-model: adlc review --providers gemini, APPROVE with no material adversarial findings on the library seam, the doors, and the landing.

dryEvidence: Frozen rails: six phase-15 and T255 rails changed by design when the store-wide write grant retired (oauth-token, oauth-revoke, oauth-cimd, admin-connections, whoami, consent-exchange). Each was pinned by sha256 of the door PR's committed bytes in the declaration PR #529, rehearsed EXEMPT six times against that branch and six violations against main from the same tree, and the entries were spent again once the door PR merged. Every other frozen rail is byte-identical. The ticket's rail set now names the whole of S1: consent-binding, consent-exchange, binding-route, connection-writes, read-scope, and the browser story rail. adlc rails-guard --ticket T262 --base HEAD --record: all checks passed.
